summary: Radar for 2026-10-18, GLP-1 focus. Three things are moving at once. (1) Retatrutide is the hottest search cluster. "Approval status", "FDA concerns" and "weight loss compared to other drugs" queries keep coming back in the news-query feeds. NY Post, Futurism and Gizmodo reported on Oct 16–17 that FDA received 2 death reports linked to bootleg products sold as retatrutide; the reports are unverified and causality is unclear. Lilly has also said all Phase 3 obesity data are in and it plans to file with FDA in Q1 2027. That fits our best lane: a calm, dated "Is retatrutide approved yet? (Oct 2026)" piece. (2) Today, Oct 18, Medical Xpress and Newsweek covered an ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 meeting abstract. It looked at 2,028,601 elective-surgery patients (145,610 on a GLP-1). GLP-1 use was linked to 11% lower odds of major heart complications and 8% lower odds of infections after surgery. It's observational, but it's emerging with almost no creator coverage, and our anesthesia Short already got 83 views. (3) Novo's lawsuit says Lilly's ads compared top-dose tirzepatide with lower semaglutide doses. Higher-dose Wegovy HD (7.2 mg, FDA-approved Mar 19, 2026) brings back the tirzepatide vs semaglutide head-to-head, which is our proven Short format. Evergreen picks with fresh hooks: the SURMOUNT-5 GI side-effects follow-up, what happens after stopping, semaglutide and alcohol (Lancet RCT), the tirzepatide eye data, and 'Ozempic face' (new systematic review, plus Lilly exploring aesthetic medicine). Rejected or kept out: Mochi/telehealth price promotion, compounded-switching how-tos, 'does tirzepatide cause breast cancer' scare searches, the anorexia/telehealth story, and the low-dose tirzepatide strategy in older adults. Orforglipron stays long-form only, per our analytics. Verification gaps: Lilly's retatrutide press release returned 403, so TRIUMPH figures must be confirmed from Lilly's own releases. We don't use the third-party summary sites (compoundreview etc.). STEP UP's 20.7% is the trial-product estimand, so the scriptwriter needs the treatment-policy figure too. I couldn't find the ScienceAlert fat-cell injection story; treat it as preclinical until the primary paper is checked.

candidates.topic: Is retatrutide approved yet? (Oct 2026): all Phase 3 obesity trials reported, Lilly plans to file with FDA in Q1 2027, and it's still not approved anywhere
candidates.angle: A calm, dated status check, attributed line by line. What Lilly reported (Phase 3 weight loss in adults with obesity, or overweight with a related condition, without diabetes; state the population and timeframe for each trial). What's next: Lilly plans a US filing in Q1 2027. Status: not FDA-, MHRA-, Health Canada- or TGA-approved as of Oct 2026. Close: anything sold now isn't the trial drug, so talk to your prescriber about approved options. Title idea: 'Is retatrutide approved yet? (Oct 2026)'.

Our retatrutide Shorts have a median of 98 views (1.75× typical), and the dated status-question format gave our best Reel (85).

candidates.topic: Two deaths reported to FDA after products sold as 'retatrutide': what's confirmed and what isn't (Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: 'What's confirmed?' frame. FDA received 2 death reports linking the deaths to products claiming to be retatrutide (a 41-year-old in July, a 49-year-old reported last month). The reports are unverified and don't prove the product caused the deaths. The real trial drug is not approved, and products sold online aren't the trial drug. Lilly's CMO said black-market versions are 'not a medicine', and Lilly has filed lawsuits against sellers. End with: talk to a prescriber about approved options. No seller names, no buying info, no emoji.

candidates.topic: Having surgery on Ozempic or Mounjaro? ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 study of 2 million surgical patients linked GLP-1 use to 11% lower odds of major heart complications and 8% lower odds of infections
candidates.angle: A positive, practical Short. A huge records study (2,028,601 adults having elective surgery over 60 minutes with a hospital stay of 24 h or more; 145,610 on a GLP-1, matched to similar non-users) linked GLP-1 use to fewer heart complications and infections after surgery. It's observational: the lead author says more research is needed to know if the drug drives it. Pair it with the practical point: tell your surgical and anesthesia team you're on a GLP-1. Title idea: 'Surgery on a GLP-1 like Mounjaro: safer for your heart?'
candidates.why_now: Published today (Oct 18) via Medical Xpress and Newsweek ('Millions of surgery records reveal a potential new benefit'). Supporting PubMed studies on knee (J Knee Surg, Oct 15), shoulder and hip arthroplasty. Our anesthesia Short reached 83 views. Creator coverage is still near zero.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) vs higher-dose semaglutide (Wegovy HD 7.2 mg): does the new dose close the gap? Context for Novo's lawsuit over Lilly's ads
candidates.angle: A named head-to-head with honest framing. SURMOUNT-5 compared tirzepatide with semaglutide 2.4 mg head-to-head (tirzepatide 20.2% vs semaglutide 13.7%, 72 weeks, adults with obesity without diabetes). Wegovy HD 7.2 mg (FDA-approved Mar 19, 2026) showed 20.7% in STEP UP, but that was a different trial against placebo, so it isn't a head-to-head. That's exactly what Novo's lawsuit argues about. Explain why cross-trial numbers can't crown a winner. Include the 'don't switch or stop on your own' line.
keywords: which is stronger Wegovy or Mounjaro
